motivation: The real apache/logging-chainsaw adaptation is test-only (allowTypes added inside the failing test; ~10 production usages left unadapted). This authored mimic reproduces the SAME break with the adaptation in PRODUCTION code, so it demonstrates the production-side fix the chainsaw case lacks.

in_repo_version_transition.mechanism: authored mimic — no real repository history
in_repo_version_transition.evidence: Self-contained authored project; the 1.4.17 -> 1.4.19 transition is set synthetically by the differential, not a real in-repo commit.

bump_source.comment: Break characterized from BUMP; the failing test here is derived from the BUMP failing test.

behavioral_break.why_it_breaks: xstream 1.4.18 switched its security framework to default-deny: classes not on an explicit allowlist are rejected on unmarshalling. save()/toXML compiles and runs; load()/fromXML throws ForbiddenClassException at runtime -> behavioural break, not syntactic.

adaptation.summary: The production XStream factory (PreferenceStore.newXStream) allowlists the deserialized domain type to satisfy xstream >=1.4.18 default-deny. The test contains no XStream security config, so a green run proves production code was adapted (contrast the chainsaw case, which fixed only the test).

verification.method: 3-state differential build+test with Maven on JDK 11; xstream version swapped via -Dxstream.version, production adaptation toggled via -Dmimic.adapt
verification.conclusion: Confirmed BBC with a production-side adaptation: a passing test breaks only under xstream >=1.4.18 with otherwise-unchanged code, and allowlisting the type in production code resolves it.

external_mining_note: GitHub mining for a real external production adaptation surfaced Apache ActiveMQ (AMQ-8358 upgrade to 1.4.18). Its production XStream whitelist (activemq-stomp XStreamSupport.java, addPermission/allowTypesByWildcard) was added earlier in commit 6f03921b for AMQ-6013 ('restrict classes which can be serialized inside the broker') as PROACTIVE hardening, NOT triggered by the 1.4.18 bump — so at upgrade time only a test (SamplePojo) needed fixing. This is the confounded-signature false-positive mode documented in the methodology: xstream allowTypes co-occurs with general RCE hardening. Hence the authored mimic is used to demonstrate the production-side fix cleanly.
